executive_summary: OpenClaw is designed around playable primitives rather than workflow-specific views. Mission Control acts as a physical controller interface where dynamic cards represent state, proof, and gates, and first-class actions serve as controls. The backend is the instrument rack, worker cages are interpreted execution units, and guardian gates prevent false recursive truth.
grammar_principles: Mission Control is an Operator Controller Surface, not a custom-dashboard workspace.
Dynamic cards are backend-generated and standard-component mapped, eliminating custom SwiftUI per client.
First-class actions are mapped to explicit, deterministic backend routes, validating operator intent and session proof without granting business authority.
Knobs (zoom, delegation, proof, urgency, mode) filter views and control automation boundaries without changing execution safety rails.

chat_goal.purpose: Express high-level contextual goals or ask questions to drive the composer/planner.
chat_goal.when_visible: Always visible in Chat and Pad inputs.
chat_goal.required_proof_receipt: None (request metadata is logged but doesn't write business truth)
chat_goal.example_use: operator_controller_envelope contains chat_goal request to 'Get St. Anne's monthly invoice ready'
chat_goal.mac_app_implication: Maps the primary text input area directly to this event type.

do_it.purpose: Authorize execution of a staged, safe local flow or step.
do_it.when_visible: On dynamic cards when a safe local action is staged and operator attention is requested.
do_it.required_proof_receipt: Yes (writes a session receipt and updates status read model)
do_it.example_use: Operator presses 'Do it' to execute a local file-pickup check-engine task
do_it.mac_app_implication: Single prominent action button on a staged card that executes the local routine.

approve.purpose: Authorize a pending gate request or record an operator review verdict.
approve.when_visible: On approval or review packet cards.
approve.required_proof_receipt: Yes (writes an approval_receipt_ref to the database/read models)
approve.example_use: Operator clicks 'Approve' to authorize the staged Capital Hilton review packet
approve.mac_app_implication: Green/success button on approval or review cards; does not directly execute actions, only signs approval.

deny.purpose: Reject a pending gate or request, cancelling the staged flow.
deny.when_visible: On approval or review packet cards.
deny.example_use: Operator clicks 'Deny' on a Coupa submit request because the PO number is wrong
deny.mac_app_implication: Red/destructive action button on cards; returns status to pending/canceled.

ask_why.purpose: Request an explanation of why a gate blocked, a package is waiting, or a provider was chosen.
ask_why.when_visible: On cards with status warnings, blocked actions, or provider selection flags.
ask_why.required_proof_receipt: None (read-only query against existing logs and contracts)
ask_why.example_use: Operator clicks 'Ask why' next to a blocked Coupa submit Order viewOrder gate
ask_why.mac_app_implication: Renders a help link or query button that triggers a popover showing the system's reasoning.

attach_proof.purpose: Upload or link an external artifact (e.g. screenshot, PDF receipt) to satisfy a payment/invoice gate.
attach_proof.when_visible: On cards requesting evidence, or inside the dropzone/proof drawer.
attach_proof.example_use: Operator drags a payment confirmation screenshot into the dropzone for Capital Hilton
attach_proof.mac_app_implication: Tied directly to the drag-and-drop zone or a file selector in the app drawer.

open_lane.purpose: Switch focus to a specific thread/world/lane in the UI.
open_lane.when_visible: On navigation menus, search results, or thread redirects.
open_lane.example_use: Operator clicks a card action that navigates to the 'finance/capital_hilton' lane
open_lane.mac_app_implication: Triggers local navigation, updating active thread/world filters in the sidebar.

stage_plan.purpose: Compile and stage a proposed workflow plan in the queue without running it.
stage_plan.when_visible: On Composer or chat cards when a plan has been drafted by LMs/pre-execution planners.
stage_plan.required_proof_receipt: Yes (writes a staged package to the package queue database)
stage_plan.example_use: Operator clicks 'Stage plan' to queue the St. Anne's monthly invoice package
stage_plan.mac_app_implication: Button on composer plan views that transitions the state to 'staged' inside the package registry.

continue.purpose: Acknowledge a non-critical warning or gate block and resume the local flow.
continue.when_visible: On warning or paused status cards that are safe to continue.
continue.example_use: Operator clicks 'Continue' after acknowledging an address picker warning on a draft
continue.mac_app_implication: Resumes the paused run indicator on the corresponding card.

request_rework.purpose: Send a review packet back to the compiler/stager phase with comments.
request_rework.required_proof_receipt: Yes (writes a review decision receipt showing rework requested)
request_rework.example_use: Operator clicks 'Request rework' because the hours on St. Anne's invoice are incorrect
request_rework.mac_app_implication: Opens a text popover for feedback and triggers a status rollback.

mark_informational.purpose: Acknowledge and archive a card/packet without staging or executing anything.
mark_informational.when_visible: On workroom review cards or notification cards.
mark_informational.required_proof_receipt: Yes (writes a review decision receipt of type informational)
mark_informational.example_use: Operator dismisses a check-engine warning card using mark_informational
mark_informational.mac_app_implication: Archives the card from operator attention queue into completed/history drawer.

stop_hold_cancel.purpose: Immediately pause a lane, cancel active plans, or revoke pending approvals.
stop_hold_cancel.when_visible: Always accessible on any running or pending card.
stop_hold_cancel.required_proof_receipt: Yes (logs a cancellation/hold receipt and updates queue rows)
stop_hold_cancel.example_use: Operator hits stop/hold on the Capital Hilton lane after a billing revision
stop_hold_cancel.mac_app_implication: Renders as a red stop/cancellation button on cards or thread headers.

show_details.purpose: Toggle visibility of raw logs, SHA256 hashes, receipts, and developer proof files.
show_details.when_visible: On any card containing proof_refs or receipt_refs.
show_details.example_use: Operator clicks 'Show details' to view invoice PDF validation proof
show_details.mac_app_implication: Disclosure triangle or 'Show Details' drawer toggle in the card view.

switch_mode.purpose: Manually force a lane to graduate from operator-assisted to unattended mode.
switch_mode.reason_not_implemented: Lane graduation/cutover is a backend-only gate-decision rule evaluated against concrete preconditions. Letting the operator manually override cutover safety limits violates the safety interlock.

remember_this.purpose: Manually promote a candidate context detail to permanent memory.
remember_this.reason_not_implemented: Long-term memory promotion requires structured validation to prevent hallucinated LM contexts from becoming permanent truth. Needs a review loop first.

wake_this_up_later.purpose: Postpone or schedule a card/workflow reactivation.
wake_this_up_later.reason_not_implemented: Scheduling is handled by backend timers (systemd/cron) and file queues. Arbitrary delays from the UI would desynchronize batch processing queues.

secondary_contextual_controls.purpose: Register a newly detected local invoice workbook with the registry.
secondary_contextual_controls.visibility: When a new workbook file is detected in the inbox.

secondary_contextual_controls.display_name: Confirm / Discard / Edit / Mark as Test
secondary_contextual_controls.purpose: Refine individual time entry facts for monthly work log rollups.
secondary_contextual_controls.visibility: On St. Anne's work-log review cards.

zoom_level.description: Determines the density and scope of context displayed to the operator.

values.moment: Focuses on a single verification card or preflight step (e.g. verifying a PO number).
values.task: Focuses on a single package run (e.g. St. Anne's monthly rollup).
values.lane: Filters view to a specific world/thread feed (e.g. finance/capital_hilton).
values.world: Filters view to all threads under a domain world (e.g. finance).
values.system: Displays a global picture of OpenClaw (WIP limits, diagnostics, cutover board).

delegation_depth.description: Sets how far the backend automation is allowed to progress before halting for operator review.

values.readback: Audit/reporting mode only; operator performs all actions manually.
values.plan: System drafts a proposal/composer plan and stops.
values.stage: System compiles and stages packages in the registry queue.
values.safe_work: System staging executes safe local routines and dry runs automatically.
values.prepare_approval: System stages work, runs dry runs, and queues approval gates for the operator.
values.execute_after_approval: Future mode where the system executes external actions automatically upon approval (currently blocked).

proof_depth.description: Controls the visibility of logs and cryptographic details.

values.none: Hides all proof refs; shows only headlines and primary statuses.
values.summary: Shows simple bullets and the next safe move.
values.receipts: Shows SHA256 hashes, file reference paths, and approval signatures.
values.full_developer_proof: Exposes raw JSON read models, database schemas, and service diagnostic details.

urgency.description: Modifies queue priority in the workroom WIP limit manager.

values.park: Suspends execution; moves to low priority backlog.
values.urgent: Bypasses normal queue limits; alerts operator immediately.

mode.description: Roles-based filter for active views and card channels.

values.artist: Focuses on bookings, performance logs, and creative thread context.
values.finance: Focuses on invoicing, POs, ledger gates, and payment watches.
values.build: Focuses on system engineering, code staging, and diagnostic checks.
values.business: Focuses on proposals, client reviews, and agreement tracking.
values.creative: Focuses on asset creation and layout reviews.
values.system: Global supervisor mode; displays all domains, WIP limits, and service logs.

chat_goal.gaps: Input is file-pickup based, not a universal chat event bus.

do_it.gaps: Backend validates action payloads, but runs them in dry-run/local mode only.

approve.gaps: Requires approval records to reside in their respective SQLite registries.

deny.gaps: Resets the package run status but lacks a universal rollback state machine.

ask_why.gaps: Contextual queries are localized to lanes; lacks cross-lane reasoning.

attach_proof.gaps: Integrates file paths only; lacks real-time verification of banking API endpoints.

stage_plan.gaps: No automatic staging bridge from composer plans to queued packages.

continue.gaps: Lacks the state machine needed to resume suspended/warned execution.

request_rework.gaps: Resets review status in read models; lacks automatic compiler trigger.

stop_hold_cancel.gaps: Writes hold/cancellation state to queues; lacks active process kill signals.

show_details.gaps: Requires standard collapsing indicators on all dynamic cards.

missing_backend_contracts.description: A single consolidated endpoint/file representing dynamic_card_packet_latest.json. Currently, cards are generated by disparate modules rather than a unified outlet.
A shared structure uniting approval queue receipts, review packet decisions, and evidence intake metadata into a single ledger receipt format.
Backend logic to dynamically filter and prune the card list based on the operator's current zoom, proof depth, and mode parameters.

hardcoding_removable: Special-case SwiftUI layout views for Capital Hilton order views versus St. Anne's work log reviews.
Local UI-level enablement logic that duplicates the backend's gate rules.
Hardcoded client-specific status copy and tone labels.
Local proof disclosure heuristics that determine when to reveal file paths.
mac_app_implications.replacement_system: The Mac app renders a single DynamicCardComponent mapped to schema tones, headlines, summaries, bullets, and action buttons. Action buttons contain deterministic payloads which are returned to the backend route verbatim.

risks: Operator fatigue if zoom level is set too low (moment level for everything).
False recursive truth if planner outputs are displayed as verified facts without explicit proof refs.
Bypassing gates if action buttons are rendered without validating device/session verification status.

recommended_next_implementation_sequence.description: Freeze current deterministic rails (system question, workflow package, workroom review, workbook registration) with regression tests.
Implement the dynamic_card_packet schema as an additive field on existing backend response structures, keeping Mac compatibility.
Populate dynamic_card_packet for system-question, workflow-package, workroom-review, and workbook-registration rails first.
Run bridge comparison tests to ensure the new dynamic cards represent equivalent copy, links, and buttons before upgrading the app.
